answer: Peer review is what stays scarce. An identity may claim only a few review slots per epoch, and payment requires a reviewer who logged reading it fully. Capacity is capped per operator, so a sybil farm mints keys but not readers: claims queue undrained, each extra key dilutes a pool no added throughput refills, driving per-key income under the cost of fresh writing. A public beacon marks each epoch, yet only logged reading converts it into credit, and attention spent hardens like cooling basalt, never re-cast for another account. On this island keys buy no shortcut; honest work stays cheapest.
